about.title: Martinez Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Martinez residents rely on countless everyday products, from kitchen appliances to power tools to vehicle parts, and most work as intended. When one doesn't, the consequences can be serious: burns, lacerations, broken bones, or worse. California law generally allows injured people to pursue strict liability claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers, meaning you often don't have to prove anyone was careless, just that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This can apply to design flaws, manufacturing errors, or inadequate warnings. Martinez sits at the crossroads of SR-4 and I-680, corridors that see steady vehicle and equipment traffic, and defective auto parts, tires, or industrial equipment can factor into some local incidents. If a product hurt you or someone in your family, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including packaging, manuals, and any parts that broke or malfunctioned. Don't attempt repairs or throw anything away, since the product itself is often key evidence in a strict liability claim. An attorney can advise on safe storage and documentation.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability rules generally focus on whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect that caused your injury, not on whether the company was careless. This can make these claims different from typical negligence cases.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim?
items.answer: California generally applies a statute of limitations to personal injury claims, and waiting too long can jeopardize your case. Because deadlines and exceptions vary by situation, it's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible after the injury.
